Definition lines 40–42 uses the gradient at the second argument. R(1)=1/2 and derivative R prime(1)=1 give T_y(t)=t-1/2. The drawn tangent segment from (0.5,0) to (3.6,3.1) has slope 1 and passes through (1,0.5), matching the derivative of the parabola there.

At x=3 the marked tangent point is (3,2.5) and curve point is (3,4.5). Their vertical difference is 2=B_R(3||1) by line 42. The double-headed dimension arrow at offset t=3.12 spans those same heights; it denotes a scalar gap. Dashed projections identify y=1 and x=3.

Line 46 with H_R=H_R inverse=1 yields absolute-value primal/dual norms, as captioned. The curves are only a window into functions defined on all R, explicitly stated in the caption; drawn ends assert no domain boundary. Three solid disks denote included function values; no open endpoints or graph cycles are asserted. The definition and rigorous mathematical content remain independent of the illustration.
